title: Welcome to Mogul Workspace
text: Welcome to Mogul Workspace, the web tool for preparing quotations at Mogul Electromech. In this video we'll go through everything: signing in, the dashboard, making a quotation from a customer's enquiry, printing and emailing it, recording the order or a lost quote, and finding your quotations later.

title: Signing in
text: Open the workspace link in your browser. Your admin gives you a username and a temporary password. Type them in, and click Sign In.

title: Set your own password
text: The first time, you're asked to set your own password. Type the temporary password, then your new password twice, and click Save Password. After five wrong attempts, the account locks for fifteen minutes.

title: Dashboard
text: This is your Dashboard. At the top: the value you quoted, the purchase orders received, your win rate, and how many quotations are still waiting for the customer's reply. Switch the period here: seven days, four weeks, three months or twelve months.

title: Dashboard
text: Follow-Up Required lists sent quotations with no reply yet, and how old they are. Below are the values by customer, lost value by reason, and your largest quotations. You only see your own quotations. Admins see everyone's.

title: Finding your way
text: On the left: New Quotation, the Dashboard, Quotations and Customers. At the bottom is your name. Click it to change your password or sign out. Let's make a new quotation.

title: Customer
text: First, the customer. Start typing the name, and the list filters as you type. Pick the customer, and their address, attention, payment terms, validity, delivery and VAT terms are filled in from the customer's saved details. You can still change them for this quotation.

title: New customer
text: If the customer is new, choose New Customer at the bottom of the list. Fill in their details once, and they are saved for next time.

title: Enquiry, Sales Rep and date
text: Next, the enquiry reference. The Sales Rep is you, by default, and the date is today. Check the Attention name for this enquiry.

title: Paste the items
text: Now the items. You don't need to type them. In the customer's Excel sheet, select the rows and copy them. Then come back to the quotation, and press Control V.

title: Import Preview
text: The Import Preview opens. The app found the header row and mapped each column: description, quantity and unit. Part numbers and make are added to the description, and section headings are kept. It also found the enquiry reference. If a column is mapped wrong, change it here. Then click Add lines.

title: Import a PDF, screenshot or email
text: Enquiries also come as PDFs, screenshots or emails. Click Import File, or drop the file on the lines. Here's a PDF. The original is shown beside the lines, so you can check them. You can also paste a screenshot with Control V. Prices in the customer's file are always ignored.

title: Enter the rates
text: Now enter the rates. The first rate cell is already selected. Type the rate and press Enter, and you move down to the next line. The amounts and totals update as you go, and lines without a rate are counted in orange.

title: Editing lines
text: The lines work like a spreadsheet. Use the arrow keys to move, and type to replace a cell. Each line has a menu: insert a line or a section, duplicate, move or delete. Control D copies the cell above, and Control Z undoes.

title: Remarks and internal notes
text: Remarks are printed on the quotation. Internal Notes are only for us, and never printed.

title: Save
text: Now click Save, or press Control S. The quotation gets its number when you first save it, for example M E, twenty-six, zero zero seven.

title: Workings
text: Workings is for your costing: photos, supplier prices or screenshots. On a phone, tap Add File to use the camera. Workings are internal and never printed.

title: Print / PDF
text: Click Print, PDF. You see the quotation exactly as the customer will, on the Mogul letterhead, with the T R N, the stamp, and the amount in words. Click Print, and choose Save as PDF. The file is already named with the quotation number and the customer.

title: Email
text: To send it, click Email. The customer's email, the copy, the subject and the message are filled in from your template. Click Open in Outlook, attach the PDF, and send. The email is logged on the quotation.

title: Lost quotations
text: When the customer replies, record the result. If we lost it, click Mark as Lost, choose the reason, such as price or delivery time, and add a note. Lost reasons show on the Dashboard.

title: Record the order
text: When the purchase order arrives, click Record Order. Enter the PO number and date, attach the PO copy, and tick the lines they ordered. Change the quantity or rate if the PO is different. Click Save, and the quotation is marked Won, or Partly Won.

title: More actions
text: The three dots open more actions. Create Revision makes REV zero one with the same number, and keeps the old version read-only. Duplicate copies it into a new quotation. You can also cancel a quotation, or delete a draft.

title: Quotations
text: The Quotations page lists your quotations. Search by number, customer, enquiry reference, or even item text. Filter by Sales Rep, status or date. Ordered amounts show in green. And Export to Excel gives you the list as a spreadsheet.

title: Customers
text: Under Customers, you see everyone we quote, with their default terms. Click a customer to edit them. These terms are copied onto every new quotation for that customer.

title: For admins: Users
text: The last two pages are for admins. On Users, the admin adds each person, with their email, phone and email template, and resets passwords. Every user can also be picked as a Sales Rep.

title: For admins: Settings
text: Settings holds the company letterhead details, the quotation number prefix, VAT, currency, and the default terms for new customers.

title: That's it!
text: That's everything. To recap: pick the customer, paste or import the items, enter the rates, save, then print and email. And when the customer replies, record the order, or the reason we lost it. Happy quoting!
